T H A R R O S / C A N A D A Data Note · TC-2026-001
1
Analytical Report: Traffic Collisions by Location 2017-2024
(excluding 2023)
By Magnus Abdelnour
Published September 16, 2026 · Tharros Canada · tharros.ca/research/id/TC-2026-001
Overview
Published August 14, 2026, Traffic Collisions by Location 2017-2024 (excluding 2023) is a dataset
collected and maintained by the City of Ottawa, provided to the public under the Open Data Licence
Version 2.0, detailing all traffic collisions between 2017-2024 (excluding 2023) in the Ottawa region.1 A
total of 94,406 traffic incidents were documented. Collision information is collected via motor vehicle
collision reports submitted by the Ottawa police and provided to the city for inclusion in its collision
database.2 This dataset provides collision information, including the severity and number of victims,
aiding city planning officials in making educated decisions in relation to road policy changes or
additions to certain roads and routes to prevent future collisions.
Technical Contents
Each incident entry contains the incident’s date, exact coordinates, year, intersection/road the
incident occurred on, accident classification, impact type, road surface condition, environmental
condition, light/time of day, and traffic control (Figure 1). Furthermore, it contains data on the number
of vehicles, pedestrians, bicycles, motorcycles involved, as well as injuries and the level of severity
from minimal to fatal. This dataset is updated and reviewed annually and has its metadata readily
available. However, I found no separate data dictionary or methodological guide.3 The data can be
accessed online through the City of Ottawa website, and can be viewed in three different forms: an
embedded Geo-map, a Tabular Data View or an ArcGIS Feature Layer. It can be accessed and
downloaded/shared via CSV, Shapefile, GeoJSON, and KML. Downloading the data via CSV was the
most efficient method; after the small pop-up window that appears when the download button is
pressed, I was able to open the table in Excel. The dataset is provided under the City of Ottawa Open

Data Licence Version 2.0, which allows copying, modification, publication and commercial use as long
as it’s for lawful purposes with proper attribution and accreditation. 4
Quality & Limitations
The dataset provides detailed information on 94,406 reported traffic collisions across Ottawa from
2017 to 2024 (excluding 2023). It uses official police collision reports and City validation procedures,
providing a strong basis for reliability and transparency. The data is clearly structured and can be
filtered by variables such as location, collision type and injury severity, making it accessible for a wide
range of analyses. However, the complete absence of 2023 creates a significant gap and limits the
dataset’s usefulness for continuous 2017 to 2024 trend analysis.
Fit for Use Assessment
This dataset is fit to be used for needs pertaining to geographic distribution, characteristics, and
trends in reported traffic collisions in the City of Ottawa. While the dataset is well suited for identifying
broader collision trends across Ottawa, the absence of 2023 limits its reliability for continuous
analysis and weakens any findings and conclusions that depend on complete 2017 to 2024
comparisons.
